newsitem.title: UK: YEAREND-French stocks seen up nine pct by end-97.
newsitem.headline: YEAREND-French stocks seen up nine pct by end-97.

text.p: French equities are expected to show a lacklustre performance at the start of 1997 but the Paris bourse should improve towards the end of the year, according to a Reuters poll of forecasts for the world's top 15 bourses.

The survey of nine analysts who follow French stocks showed that the benchmark CAC-40 index of blue chips was expected to rise to 2,450 by the end of 1997. This represents a rise of nearly nine percent on Tuesday's close of 2,251.40.
The highest forecast for the CAC-40 was 2,600 and the lowest was 2,200.
Following is a selection of views on next year's performance of the Paris stock exchange:
GARY DUGAN, EQUITY STRATEGIST AT J.P. MORGAN
"We think the year will start badly for France and will gradually improve through the year, with accelerating growth and the persistance of low inflation."
MICHELLE JARDIN, EQUITY STRATEGIST AT CREDIT LYONNAIS SECURITIES
"The trend in the French stock market in 1997 will be conditioned by the ability of the economy to show clearer signs of recovery and the consequent effects on companies' profits."
